title: Genuina principia doctrinae de statu aequilibrii et motu corporum tam perfecte flesibilium quam elasticorum

deep.reconstruction:
Context: Euler sets up general balance equations for a planar thread or rod. T is the tangential force (tension), V the normal (shear) force, p and q the tangential and normal loads per unit length, φ the tangent angle and s the arc length. The bending moment is Vv, where v is a lever arm. The equations are (I) dT + V dφ = p ds, (II) dV − T dφ = q ds, (III) d(Vv) = V ds, together with a constitutive law for the moment.

Case 3 (finishing from the previous page): the stiffness S(s) varies along the rod, because of varying thickness or material. The moment law is Vv = S dφ/ds. Taking ds constant, (III) gives V = (S ddφ + dS dφ)/ds², i.e. V = (Sκ)' with κ = dφ/ds. Substituting into (I) gives dT = p ds − (S dφ ddφ + dS dφ²)/ds², i.e. T' = p − κ(Sκ)'. Euler remarks that this cannot be integrated in closed form even if ∫p ds is known. In the uniform case it integrates to T = ∫p ds − Aκ²/2; here S κ (Sκ)' is not an exact derivative unless S is constant. From (II), T = (S d³φ + 2 dS ddφ + ddS dφ)/(ds² dφ) − q ds/dφ, i.e. T = ((Sκ)'' − q)/κ. Equating the derivative of this T with the first expression gives the shape equation [((Sκ)'' − q)/κ]' = p − κ(Sκ)'. This is a fourth-order ODE for φ(s), which Euler declines to write out in general.

Case 4 (begun here, continued on the next page): the rod is naturally curved, with radius of curvature r(s) in its unstressed state. Section XVII starts the argument that the moment needed is proportional only to the excess of the actual curvature dφ/ds over the natural curvature 1/r. Hence Vv = A(dφ/ds − 1/r), the intrinsic-curvature constitutive law of the planar Euler–Kirchhoff rod.
errors: No mathematical errors on this page. The derivative d[(S ddφ + dS dφ)/ds²] = (S d³φ + 2dS ddφ + ddS dφ)/ds² (ds constant) is correct, and so is the remark on non-integrability.
Minor figure inconsistency: the margin note reads Tab. VII Fig. 4, but the text says 'Sit igitur figura 2'. Fig. 1 is then used for the deformed shape.

ideas.what: Equilibrium of a rod with arc-length-dependent bending stiffness: V = (Sκ)', T' = p − κ(Sκ)', T = ((Sκ)'' − q)/κ
ideas.modern_name: Planar Euler–Kirchhoff rod equations with nonuniform bending stiffness EI(s)
ideas.usually_credited_to: Euler (1744 for elastica statics; this 1771 paper for the general force-balance formulation, per Truesdell)
ideas.where_published: E410, Novi Comm. Acad. Sci. Petrop. 15 (1771); nonuniform laminae also appear in E65 (1744)

ideas.what: Moment proportional to the difference between actual and natural curvature
ideas.modern_name: Intrinsic (spontaneous) curvature in the Kirchhoff rod / bending energy (κ − κ0)²
ideas.usually_credited_to: Euler (also Jacob Bernoulli's ideas); standard in Truesdell's history
ideas.where_published: E410; naturally curved laminae are, I believe, already treated in E65 Additamentum I (unsure of exact section)

ideas.what: Remark that the tangential balance has a first integral T + Aκ²/2 = ∫p ds only for uniform stiffness
ideas.modern_name: Conservation law / first integral of the elastica (Kirchhoff analogue)
ideas.where_published: E410, earlier cases of this paper

deep.surprise_reason: These are standard derivations from a paper Truesdell analyzed in detail. Variable stiffness and intrinsic curvature are both known Euler contributions. Nothing unfinished or uncredited beyond Euler's routine decision not to write out the fourth-order shape equation.
transcription_corrections: In the dT formula the image has capital S (the stiffness function): dT = p ds − (S dφ ddφ + dS dφ²)/ds². The transcription's lowercase 's' and 'ds' as the differential of s are misreadings; it is dS.
In the T formula, likewise: T = (S d³φ + 2 dS ddφ + ddS dφ)/(ds²·dφ) − q ds/dφ. Capital S and dS, ddS; not s, ds, dds.
Margin note 'Tab. VII. Fig. 4.' sits beside §XVI.
